label: Capacity for conscious relationship at…: Cognitive and affective capacity at the indicated world…
term: capacity for conscious relationship at a time
definition: Cognitive and affective capacity at the indicated world, person and time for reciprocal conscious interaction recognizing the other party. This is a capacity, not possession of belief or actual relationship. Not all humans at all times are assumed capable; the existential premise supplies its own witness.
note: Explicit interpretation vocabulary for #252. Source claims retain their own pinned locators; these records do not add axioms or establish the truth of the interpreted predicates.

formal_gap.meaning: Sig.Capable w p t says that, at world w, person p has at time t the cognitive and affective capacity for reciprocal conscious interaction that recognizes the other party. It is a capacity, not belief or an actual relationship. It is a field of the hiddenness signature (TruthCore.Hiddenness.Vocabulary.Sig, #252), indexed by world, person and time and supplied by each interpretation; worlds carry no modal accessibility laws.
examples: An adult of ordinary cognitive development, at a time when that development is present.
exclusions: Holding the belief (Believes) or having immediate access to the relationship just by trying (Available); access is itself not being in the relationship, since access can hold while Accepts fails.
Having the concept of a personal God (HasConcept), a separate predicate.
An infant, or a person at a time when the capacity is absent: not all humans at all times are assumed capable.
open_obligations: The empirical premise NonresistantNonbelief supplies its own capable witness at the actual world; that premise is open.
These records add no axioms; whether the interpreted predicate holds of real persons is not established by any finite model.
